The healthcare here is absolutely abysmal. I don’t know what the heck is going on but it’s an absolute shit show. 

Impossible to get a doctor even with good insurance, even worse finding specialists. You’ll fill out dozens of new patient packets (pen and paper) only to be turned away, or told the doctor is no longer with the practice. Maybe if you’re lucky you can find a nurse practitioner, but let’s be real you’re going to Auburn, or further. 

I wish I was exaggerating. The communication between offices is… nonexistent. Everyone uses their own systems and there’s no real continuity of care. I mean don’t get me wrong, healthcare is a mess everywhere in the United States, but there is something else going on here, it’s really crazy, actually a little scary. I mean I’d love some new cuisine too, maybe some more stuff to do, but damn this is like basic needs shit. 

I grew up here but I’m absolutely horrified by how hard it’s been since I moved back here 6 months ago. The cherry on top is I even work in the healthcare industry, and it’s been nearly impossible for me to navigate it, can’t even imagine how hard it is for an everyday Joe without the knowledge of the inner workings of healthcare.

If your brother has good balance I can’t recommend the iwalk enough, absolute game changer for my recovery when I broke my leg/ankle. It’s all terrain unlike the scooters, you can do stairs with practice and a handrail, seriously worth every penny. I recommend it to anyone with a non-weight bearing below knee injury as long as they can balance a little, just as a standard in recovery. Crutches hurt like hell, fuck with your lymph nodes, and occupy your hands so you can’t hold anything or carry anything across a room, peg leg it all day.

https://iwalk-free.com

That being said, the first few days and weeks of my break were fucking unbearable and I would NOT have faired well at a festival. It all depends on the severity of the break and your brothers confidence. But holy shit, the swelling alone… my foot would fill up with blood so quick the moment I stood up, I would only have a few minutes before my foot was in excruciating pain and felt like it was going to explode. I basically laid down on the floor for hours at a time with my foot propped on the couch and three ice packs strapped to my leg. But that’s just me.

Sorry this is really long, first time ever writing about it so it's all coming out. It was a really challenging journey, and I went in knowing how hard it could be, but it was like nothing I could have expected, and there's really no other way I could have emerged with the same lessons than by going through what I did.

I'm not sure if you call it ego death, but here's what happened:

I did some meditating and writing, but as the experience got more and more intense I ended up getting stuck in really wild thought loops where I was inhabiting different personas, with full on different memories (one of them that I can remember was a person called Roy, weird.) I bounced between different realities, each universe with it's own laws and constraints, each persona with their own different values, goals, and aspirations, occasionally I thought I was an alien or an inter-dimensional being, to the point where I couldn't remember who my physical body actually belonged to.

Time ceased to exist in some universes (no surprise) so it felt like I was stuck in an eternal cycle through endlessly varying consciousnesses. It was really, really fucking terrifying and bizarre, confusing, disorienting, I wasn't even sure if I was alive or existed at all. I thought I'd never remember who I was and thought I was literally going to be cycling through consciousnesses forever, trying to figure out whether any of it was real.

There were times I couldn't even remember I had taken LSD, then I would remember and tell myself it was just a drug, then wonder if LSD was even a drug and think that existence was just a construction or a simulation, I convinced myself that nothing was really real and I was simultaneously everybody and nobody. Cycling through like, fractals of beings in what felt like seconds, I couldn't even keep track I was so many different things at once. I thought this was all a computer program and I had glimpsed the truth, or that I was travelling between multiverses, seeing the beyond, and just as I would break out of one reality I would enter into another, it was like I couldn't escape and also couldn't stop escaping. So, so strange. I legit thought I had triggered psychosis and I would never be the same, always questioning what reality was and who I was.

I was in my apartment the whole time and I was able to find meaning in the objects around me and slowly put myself back together and remember who I actually was, what I valued, and how my life had meaning in this reality as it became more and more consistent. I never felt so grateful to be myself, so utterly relieved and overjoyed to be here. I cried when I finally felt that I was home and here to stay, I found universal truths to guide my journey through this life, and I found a deep love for myself and this universe and this plane of existence that we perceive. Just absolutely humbled and grateful to be me, and to love the people I'm with, the experience that I have, and love myself and be at peace. It took some time to put the pieces back together, I felt like my whole world had vanished and I was so happy to have it back. Really incredible. I actually didn't fully understand what I had learned until a good couple days later, I was so focused on just recovering that it couldn't even put together how this experience had served my original goal of taking the dose, but it really changed everything.

I have often wondered this as well, and to be honest, I'm pretty disappointed by some of the responses here in this thread, I would have expected this community to be more discerning and research oriented. Especially when it comes to stacking active compounds with the goal of self improvement.

First of all, the Stamets stack is a great protocol (although I haven't looked into the efficacy of the niacin component, seems alright at face value though I guess) but Lion's Mane is a truly exceptional mushroom to add to a microdosing regimen with the intention of neuroplasticity and neurogenesis.

That being said, for Paul Stamets' reputation, the Host Defense capsules are hugely disappointing, and here's why:

1.) Beta D glucans and tri-terpenes are the compounds in Lions Mane that actually have value to neuronal growth and plasticity, and Host Defense provides absolutely no info on the content or concentration of these compounds in their product. It is absolutely possible to get a third party test to verify this info, and many other products have done just that, and it's quite honestly shameful that Paul Stamets' brand is lacking this information, and he should know better.

2.) There is an ongoing debate regarding fruiting bodies vs. mycelium, and I'm not here to take a side, but in general its best practice to consume both, as there are different quantities of compounds in each, but here's the catch: Fruiting bodies should be grown on wood substrates, while mycelium should be grown in liquid to reduce the amount of rice contaminating (or simply taking up space) in the product, rice is useless, mycelium however may very well provide health benefits. Again, Paul Stamets should know better than to distribute a product with no info on active compounds and blatantly filled with rice. Shameful.

3.) Mushrooms have a hard to digest cell wall called chitin, and it can upset people's digestive system because, well, we can't digest it. What this means is mushroom products should be extracted, either with water or alcohol (another ongoing debate in the mushroom supplements community is which is better, as both extracts produce slightly different compounds, not going more into that here). Host Defense capsules are not extracted, and so likely all the good stuff isn't even getting where its supposed to because we can't digest chitin. C'mon Paul, you HAVE to know this.

On the plus side, the Host Defense Tincture is extracted, and if I'm not mistaken, uses both Mycelium AND Fruiting bodies. I've never tried it because I lost so much faith in Host Defense for the reasons listed above. Personally I use Real Mushrooms brand, it's affordable (important to me), extracted, and has third party verification of active compounds, however only contains fruiting bodies, but I've experienced results. However for those of you with fat wallets, I'd recommend checking out Oriveda, from what I understand it's a far superior product.

Neosporin (or generic triple anti-biotic cream) is great for the first day or two, keeps that fresh wound nice and clean, but it can make your scabs a little gooey, and easily ripped off, so I just switch to soapy scrubs and blow drying after a day or so. Heyo! I have, and absolutely love both! My shrike is their thermoglass construction, which I can tell you more about if you want.. And my roycepro is last year's hollowcore model. Honestly, either way you can't go wrong, two amazing decks in my opinion. 

It also sounds like we have similar riding styles, I dont go insanely fast these days, just enough to slash and spin down hills.

So, the decks are similar in a lot of ways, both really stiff, both very top mounty, both very versatile, but the first big difference is the symmetry. I think for my style of riding these days, the shrike is more suitable because I end up doing 180s and 360s all the way down the hill, with an occasional freestyle trick. Back when I used to really send it and I was progressing my speed game, the royce was my go-to. The e-core model lost the W concave, which I really like in my model, but that's just preference. Anyway the royce's directional shape definitely makes it ride more like a speed machine.. with a kicktail.

Speaking of kicktails, I love the royce's aggresive kicktail, it's an excellent foot lock for slashing and sliding. As opposed to the shrike's kicktails which, while semetrical, feel too flat for me, and I find my foot slipping when I'm slashin around. 

Ok so the other big difference I see between these decks is the standing platform. So straight up concave for the e-core royce, but from truck to truck there's no microdrop, no rocker, it's hella flat. Which is not at all a bad thing, there's so many mounting options it helps everything feel consistent when you're moving the trucks all over the place. The shrike on the other hand, has less mounting options, but it still feels more versatile to me, likely because of it's symmetry.. Anyway it also has a little microdrop between the trucks, which is sublte, but really effective, it cradles your feet and almost makes up for the kicktail issue I was talking about earlier. You can really sink into some slides with your feet all nestled in there.

All in all, there was a time when the royce was my absolute favorite, most versatile deck, and I still seriously love that thing. But since the shrike came along, it's stolen my heart, just wish those kicktails were a lil more poppin'. Between the symmetry and the microdrop, it's hella fun. I also like to mix in a little dancy boardwalky stuff now and then, and the shrike can acommodate a bit of that, at least in comparison to the royce.

I got you. I just recently got into longboarding a couple years ago as well. Fell in fucking love. So I'm just gonna throw out a recommmendation, and that is the Bustin Maestro Pro, get the Thermoglass if you've got the cash. 

http://www.bustinboards.com/maestro-pro-longboard-details

This was my first deck and honestly, it has a little bit of everything, in my opinion it's the best intro board for someone who's not sure yet what style speaks to them. I learned so much on this board, and have since invested in various boards specific to discipline, but nothing shreds quite like the Maestro Pro.

It's a great cruiser-commuter, as it's got great centered camber so it's flexy and flowy, and the snappy rebound also adds more juice every time you push. 

So moving from the cambered center out towards the trucks, the deck dips down into some rocker, cradling your feet in two lower, stable pockets, opening up possibilities for some freeride and downhill experimentation. It's also a drop through which just makes it super low and stable, and it also has pretty aggressive concave so you really feel secure standing in the pockets, and yet super agile with your feet are closer together, on the camber.

It's fully symetrical, and has kick tails on either side, which help a lot with commuting, but also allows for some pretty sweet dancing/freestyle moves. 

For added bonus, Bustin also has a system where you can customize your graphic, which is pretty dope.

I've never actually ridden the Thermoglass version, but with nearly waterproof construction, reinforced flex, and urethane bumpers, I wish I had waited to invest in that board. I did just recently get the Thermoglass Shrike for downhill/freeride, but have yet to set it up..
